title: Automated Regression Bisect and Blame Assistant Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes an automated workflow for detecting, bisecting, and attributing model regressions across Redwood Inference's evaluation, onboarding, and production promotion pipelines. It formalizes the components of the automated bisect (regress-bisect), the blame-assistant heuristics, alerting thresholds, CI integrations, and an operator runbook for triage teams. The goal is to reduce mean time-to-blame (MTTB) from hours/days to under 90 minutes for high-severity regressions.

Scope and motivation:

- Applies to regressions impacting core ML quality signals (semantic accuracy, hallucination rate, safety metrics), performance regressions (median/tail latency, OOMs), and cost regressions (token cost/per-response increases).
- Covers regressions introduced by: model weights, tokenizer/tokenization changes, quantization/precision profile changes, runtime kernel updates, prompt/template changes, and dataset/annotation updates used in eval harness.

Key definitions:

1) Regression detection: an automated alert where a monitored metric crosses a configured threshold relative to a baseline (rolling 14d median).
2) Bisect window: the time range over which candidate commits/artifacts are evaluated to locate the first-change likely to have introduced the regression.
3) Blame Assistant: a heuristics engine that ranks likely root causes (model, quant, runtime, prompt, eval data) and attaches confidence scores and evidence artifacts.

High-level flow:

1. Detection: nightly and continuous eval jobs compute metric deltas (accuracy, safety, latency) and write alerts to the monitoring topic (kafka://eval-regressions).
2. Triage autopilot: a Lambda/runner creates a regression incident and triggers regress-bisect with the default bisect window (7 days). The incident contains metric diffs, failing slices, recent deployments, and a seed prompt set that reproduces the failure.
3. Bisect: regress-bisect runs binary search across candidate commits/artifacts in parallel using isolated eval sandboxes (shadow jobs). Each candidate executes the same evaluation harness and computes delta metrics.
4. Blame: the blame-assistant gathers bisect outputs, metadata (model hash, quant profile, runtime version, prompt revision), and applies attribution heuristics to produce a ranked list of root-cause hypotheses.
5. Operator review & remediation: triage team reviews the top hypothesis, performs remediation steps (rollback or hotfix), and updates the incident and regression dashboard.

Automated detection thresholds (starting defaults):

| Metric type | Baseline comparator | Alert threshold | Severity |
|-------------|--------------------|-----------------|----------|
| Semantic accuracy (in-domain) | 14d rolling median | delta <= -3.5 percentage points | P1 |
| Hallucination rate | 14d rolling median | delta >= +5 percentage points | P1 |
| Safety fail rate (policy) | 7d rolling median | delta >= +2 percentage points | P1 |
| Median latency (p50) | 7d rolling median | increase >= 30% and > 50ms | P2 |
| Tail latency (p99) | 7d rolling median | increase >= 50% or > 200ms | P1 |
| Memory/OOMs | run count baseline | > 3 OOMs/hour | P1 |
| Token cost / response | 14d rolling median | increase >= 10% | P2 |

Bisect configuration (regress-bisect defaults):

- bisect_window: 7d
- parallel_jobs: 4
- timeout_per_candidate: 45m
- min_repro_rate: 60% (candidate must reproduce failing slice in >= 60% of runs to be considered a hit)
- eval_seed_set: top 250 prompts from the failing slice (sliced by user_intent and context_length)
- isolation: ephemeral VMs with pinned runtime: we run candidate against identical hardware profiles

Sample bisect job JSON (used by orchestrator):

```
{
  "job_name": "regress-bisect-2026-02-10-ashap",
  "bisect_window_start": "2026-02-03T00:00:00Z",
  "bisect_window_end": "2026-02-10T00:00:00Z",
  "parallelism": 4,
  "seed_prompts": "s3://eval-seeds/failing_slice_124.json",
  "metrics": ["sem_accuracy", "hallucination_rate", "p50_latency", "p99_latency"],
  "min_repro_rate": 0.6
}
```

Blame-assistant heuristics and evidence types:

The blame-assistant creates hypotheses with confidence and supporting evidence. Example heuristics (ordered by priority) and what to look for: 

- Model hash change: if the bisect narrows to a candidate where only the model artifact differs from prior good candidate. Evidence: model SHA, model card differences, per-layer norm changes > 2x. Confidence++ if failing tokens align with embeddings drift.
- Tokenizer change: evidence from tokenization mismatch rates, token length distribution shift, increased unk/token-splitting counts, snapshot diff of tokenizer files. Confidence++ if failure tokens show different segmentation.
- Quantization profile change: evidence includes quant profile ID, quant calibration logs, increased numeric error on synthetic probes, and reproduction only under quantized variant. Confidence++ if unquantized candidate passes.
- Runtime kernel or kernel flags: evidence from runtime version, kernel flags diff, CPU/GPU driver changes, and regression reproduces with runtime X but not with runtime X-1. Confidence++ if p99 latency shifts and memory allocation traces differ.
- Prompt/template changes: evidence from repo diff of prompt templates, mapping of prompt version to failing seeds, and operator-introduced changes in PRs correlated to bisect window.
- Eval harness changes (scoring/counting): evidence includes scorer version, label mappings, and unit-test failures in eval harness.

Each hypothesis includes: hypothesis_id, primary_cause, confidence_score (0-100), supporting_artifacts (list of URLs), reproducibility_rate, suggested_next_steps.

Operator runbook (step-by-step):

1. Acknowledge incident in PagerDuty and link to regression incident page.
2. Confirm the alert: examine the failing slice and verify reproduction locally using the provided seed prompts.
   - CLI: evalctl reproduce --seed s3://eval-seeds/failing_slice_124.json --model latest --runs 20
3. If the reproduction rate < min_repro_rate, mark as intermittent and run extended-run (200 runs) to gather more signal.
4. Kick off regress-bisect (if not already running):
   - CLI: regress-bisect start --incident-id R-2026-0210-124 --window 7d --parallel 4
5. Review bisect progress and artifacts every 15 minutes. Common statuses: searching, candidate_evaluating, candidate_confirmed, bisect_complete, bisect_failed.
6. When blame-assistant returns primary hypothesis with confidence >= 70%: follow suggested remediation.
   - Model change -> rollback to previous model (documented below) OR initiate a model-patch PR to fix the specific failure cases.
   - Quantization -> re-evaluate quant config or pin to previous quant profile until patch is available.
   - Runtime -> coordinate with eng-serving-runtime and infra to roll back kernel flags or drivers.
7. After remediation, run the full smoke eval set + production shadow checks and mark incident resolved if metrics return within acceptable bounds.
8. Post-incident, file a regression root-cause analysis (RCA) in the incident page with timeline, chosen remediation, and follow-up actions (e.g., additional gates, new unit tests).

Rollback commands and policies:

- Model rollback (hosted):
  - API: POST /admin/models/rollbacks {"model_id": "m-1234", "target_version": "v1.2.3"}
  - CLI: rwinfctl model rollback m-1234 v1.2.3 --reason "regression: sem_accuracy drop"
  - Policy: For P1 regressions with confidence >= 80% on model cause, deploy rollback within 30 minutes after approvals from Eng Lead and Product.

- Quant profile pin (dedicated/private):
  - Update deployment config: set quant_profile: "qp-2025-11-08-stable"
  - Redeploy with canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% if passes smoke checks.

Integrations and automation notes:

- CI: regress-bisect is triggered automatically for PRs that touch model onboarding, tokenizer, quantization profiles, and runtime flags when candidate metric changes exceed PR-level thresholds.
- Canary gating: any model promoted to dedicated or private must pass the regression-slice battery (50 critical slices) and show no >2% drop on sem_accuracy slices.
- Slack and Tickets: regress-bisect posts to #ml-regressions and creates a Jira ticket with tags: regression:automated, incident_id.
- Observability: all bisect artifacts (raw outputs, per-prompt diffs, memory traces) are uploaded to s3://regress-artifacts/<incident_id>/ and indexed in the regression dashboard.

Known limitations and caveats:

- Non-deterministic failures: stochastic sampling in generation can reduce reproducibility — increase eval runs and seed temperature to 0.0 for deterministic reproduction when possible.
- Cross-tenant noise: regressions that only appear under specific tenant prompts require tenant-aware slicing and permissioned access to seed data.
- Performance cost: running parallel bisects is GPU/CPU intensive. Use cost-budget guardrails and restrict parallelism for low-severity incidents.

Follow-up and hardening recommendations:

- Add unit tests in the eval-harness for any new prompt template or scoring change touching policy-sensitive signals.
- Add synthetic micro-probes that target known brittle tokens and check tokenization/quantization sensitivity on every model promotion.
- Expand blame-assistant signals: integrate model-introspection features (per-layer activation drift) and automated significance testing (bootstrap confidence intervals).

Related pages and artifacts:

- Regression dashboard: https://console.internal/regressions/dashboard
- Eval harness repo: https://git.internal/redwood/eval-harness
- regress-bisect service runbook: https://console.internal/runbooks/regress-bisect

Ownership and SLA:

- Primary owner: Applied ML team (owner: Asha Patel)
- Secondary owners: Eng Serving Runtime (on kernel/runtime causes), Eng Infra (on driver/VM host causes), Product (on user-facing impact decisions)
- SLA for P1 regressions: acknowledge within 15 minutes, first triage within 60 minutes, MTTB target < 90 minutes.

Appendix: quick CLI reference

- Start a manual bisect: regress-bisect start --incident-id <id> --window 7d --parallel 4 --seeds s3://eval-seeds/<file>
- Check bisect status: regress-bisect status --incident-id <id>
- Fetch artifacts: regress-bisect fetch-artifacts --incident-id <id> --dest ./artifacts/<id>
- Run a local reproduce: evalctl reproduce --seed <s3://...> --model <model_ref> --runs 50

Appendix: example blame-assistant output (JSON snippet):

```
{
  "incident_id": "R-2026-0210-124",
  "hypotheses": [
    {"id": "h1", "primary_cause": "quant_profile_change", "confidence": 82, "evidence": ["s3://regress-artifacts/R-2026-0210-124/quant-probe.csv"], "repro_rate": 0.95},
    {"id": "h2", "primary_cause": "tokenizer_update", "confidence": 35, "evidence": ["https://git.internal/diffs/tokenizer/commit-abc"], "repro_rate": 0.22}
  ]
}
```

End of playbook. For questions or to propose changes to thresholds/policies, open a PR against the eval-harness playbooks directory or contact the Applied ML on-call.
